$doc: MQ Research Gate — architecture & monetization atlas. Machine-readable source of truth for AI chats. Human view: docs/atlas.html. Feedback log: docs/feedback.json.

app.name: MQ Research Gate
app.oneLiner: A detective's study for the Qur'an: meaning is earned from within the text (the organic Qur'anic methodology). Notice a word, open a case on its root family, gather every place the Book uses it, form a hypothesis, then weigh the classical dictionaries.
app.stack: React + Vite + TypeScript SPA (app/) over a Hono + node:sqlite backend (server/). The research server (remote/, Hono + Postgres + Better Auth) now also serves the Qur'an corpus at /corpus. MCP server (mcp/) exposes corpus + research to an AI. Electron desktop wrapper (electron/).

principle.core: Features are ROLE-based (what you may do); resources are PLAN-based (what you may read). Your own research stays local and yours.
principle.constraint: You can only enforceably charge for what the server holds, never for what already sits on the reader's disk.
principle.consequence: The corpus and the community both live on the cloud and are plan-gated there (the admin can make either free). research.db stays on the reader's machine; the app and MCP read the corpus from the cloud.

components.name: App
components.role: Reader + investigation UI. Reads the CORPUS from the research server (${REMOTE_URL}/corpus, with the session cookie), the reader's RESEARCH from the local server (/api/v1/research), and the community from the research server. Maintainers get an Admin tab.

components.name: Local server
components.role: Owns research.db (read-write). Still serves quran.db at /api/v1 for local tools/tests, but the app no longer reads the corpus from it. Its corpus code is the SAME code the cloud runs (server/src/corpus-*.ts, two drivers).

components.name: MCP
components.role: Lets an AI study the corpus + the reader's research and propose notes/indications/board items (source='ai'). Corpus: remote by default (REMOTE_URL + REMOTE_TOKEN, reads as its user) or MQ_CORPUS=local (quran.db). Research: the local research.db the app has open, behind the write guard.

components.name: Research server
components.role: The cloud: auth (cookie or personal API token), roles, plan tiers, resource access rules, the corpus at /corpus (Postgres), the community (claims, readings, divergences), publishing, and the Admin endpoints.

components.name: Desktop
components.role: Wraps the built SPA + local server in a desktop window.

corpus (Postgres schema `corpus`).holds: Qur'an text in four scripts, per-word morphology (root/lemma/form), roots, ~10 classical lexicons, translations, search indexes. Copied from quran.db and verified exact.
corpus (Postgres schema `corpus`).load: npm run corpus:migrate (-- --verify to re-verify only). remote/src/corpus/{schema,load,verify}.ts. 294,804 rows, 143.5 MB, 18 s.
corpus (Postgres schema `corpus`).collation: every text column COLLATE "C" (= SQLite BINARY) so Arabic sorts identically.
corpus (Postgres schema `corpus`).parity: npm run corpus:parity — the SAME corpus routes over each driver, compared over HTTP. Full sweep 2026-09-26: 77,439 requests (every chapter, verse, root, root pair, word, search) — all identical. --quick samples ~3k.

quran.db.holds: The same corpus in SQLite. Now the SOURCE for corpus:migrate, the local driver (MQ_CORPUS=local, tests, offline MCP) and the parity reference. The app no longer reads it.

research.db.holds: cases + board layout, form_research (established meanings) + form_revisions, trails, notes, word_indications (+ refinements), user_root_meanings, motifs, compare_sets, settings. Plus own-outbox derived_submissions / derived_proposed_claims.
research.db.ownership: A one-row owner table (name, email, uuidv5-of-email) makes the file self-describing and portable.
research.db.aiWrites: MCP proposals are tagged source='ai' and stay proposals until the reader accepts them in the app.

accessModel.rule: Features are role-based; resources are plan-based. Everything fails closed.

roles.meaning: What you may DO. requireRole(min) in remote/src/roles.ts → 401 signed out, 403 too low.

plans.ladder: DATA: table plan_tiers (name, rank, label). Seeded free (0) < pro (100); a maintainer adds e.g. student 50, scholar 200 in the Admin tab. free is always rank 0.
plans.meaning: What you may READ. A higher rank unlocks everything a lower one does; a lapsed plan (users.plan_expires_at past) counts as free.

resources.table: resource_access (kind, key, min_plan). min_plan = a tier, 'free' (= any signed-in account), or NULL (= public, no sign-in).

whole.community: key '*' — community readings, claims, dissents, divergences, pull (default pro)

perItem.translation: key = resource id; below its tier the translation is LEFT OUT of results
perItem.lexicon: key = source (lane, lisan, …); below its tier the entries are left out of a root page

resources.noRule: An item with no rule needs only what the corpus needs.
resources.refusal: requireResource(kind) → 401 {detail} if a sign-in is needed, 402 {detail, resource, plan} if a higher plan is.

accessModel.edit: In the app: Admin tab (maintainers). Also `npm run access -- show | tier | tier-remove | corpus | community | translation | lexicon` and `npm run set-plan -w @alsiraat/remote -- <email> <tier> [days]`.
accessModel.billing: Not wired yet. A maintainer grants plans in the Admin tab (or set-plan / POST /plan). That is the single seam a payment provider slots into.

auth.cookie: Better Auth session cookie — the app (credentials: 'include').
auth.apiTokens: Personal API tokens (mqrg_…, stored as SHA-256; secret shown once) for headless clients — the MCP. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer`. Made in the app: Account → Connect an AI assistant (it prints a ready MCP config). remote/src/api-tokens.ts, session.ts. A token acts exactly as its user, so the MCP reads what that user's plan allows.

corpusCode.oneCodebase: server/src/corpus-db.ts defines CorpusDb {query, one, scalar} (async). Every corpus service (content, roots, linkages, wazn, expressions, echoes, spellings, freetext, similarity, morphology) is written once against it.
corpusCode.services: createCorpusServices(db) in server/src/corpus-services.ts; warmCorpus builds the memoised indexes (the cloud warms them at startup).
corpusCode.routes: server/src/routes/{content,roots,similarity,echoes,corpus}.ts take (services, entitlements). The local server mounts them at /api/v1; the cloud mounts the identical builders at /corpus (remote/src/corpus/serve.ts) with the plan filters as entitlements.
portableSql: a total ORDER BY wherever order is visible
DISTINCT → GROUP BY … ORDER BY MIN(id)
nullable sort keys NULLS FIRST (ASC) / NULLS LAST (DESC)
Postgres int8 counts normalised to numbers

clients.app: app/src/api/client.ts: CORPUS = ${REMOTE_URL}/corpus. A refused read announces itself (CORPUS_ACCESS_EVENT) and CorpusAccessBanner says why once, at the top: offline / sign in / needs the X plan — and 'Your access has changed, reload' after a sign-in or plan grant.
clients.mcp: mcp/src/corpus-client.ts: CorpusReads with remoteReads (HTTP, default) and localReads (MQ_CORPUS=local). 401 → 'create a token', 402 → 'needs the X plan', unreachable → 'set REMOTE_URL or MQ_CORPUS=local'. server/test/mcp-remote-corpus.test.ts runs every corpus tool on both paths: byte-identical.

mcpEnv.QF_RESEARCH_DB: research.db path (default: the repo's; the app's current file is used)

phases.title: Monetization: entitlements, live community, gated publishing
Corpus → Postgres: move + verify the data
Plan tiers as data; then 'features are role-based, resources are plan-based'
phases.summary: plan_tiers; resource_access (corpus, community whole; translation, lexicon per item) replaces corpus_policy/translation_access; publishing is role-only.

phases.title: Corpus → Postgres: port the readers
phases.summary: One corpus codebase, two drivers; the cloud serves ALL of it at /corpus. Full parity: 77,439 requests identical.

phases.title: The app reads the corpus from /corpus
The MCP reads the corpus from /corpus, as its user
phases.summary: Research stays local. Account → Connect an AI assistant mints the token.

phases.title: Admin tab in the app
phases.summary: Plan tiers, who can read (corpus, community, each translation and dictionary), people (role + plan). Maintainers only.

phases.title: Billing provider
phases.summary: Slots into the plan grant (Admin tab / set-plan) with no rework of the gates.

decisions.decision: Every feature is role-based; every resource is plan-based.
decisions.why: Maintainer's call, 2026-09-26: 'it will be easier.' One question per gate: may you DO this (role), may you READ this (plan).

decisions.decision: The corpus lives in Postgres and the cloud serves it; the app and MCP read it from /corpus.
decisions.why: The maintainer's call. Makes the corpus a gateable resource. Cost: reading needs the research server (the banner says so; MQ_CORPUS=local keeps the MCP working offline).

decisions.decision: One corpus code path over a driver interface, not a Postgres twin.
decisions.why: A twin drifts. With one codebase, parity is a property of SQL portability, proven by comparing the same routes over both drivers.

decisions.decision: research.db stays on the reader's machine; the MCP writes to it behind the guard.
decisions.why: It is the reader's irreplaceable work, and the AI-proposes → app-reviews loop needs both to see the same file.

decisions.decision: Administration is an Admin tab for maintainers, not only a CLI.
decisions.why: Maintainer's request. The CLI stays for scripting.

decisions.decision: The MCP authenticates with a personal API token and reads as its user.
decisions.why: A headless process can't hold a browser session; a revocable token keeps the plan gate honest for the AI too.

decisions.decision: A translation or lexicon above the caller's tier is left out, not refused.
decisions.why: One verse carries many translations; refusing the whole page for one locked item would be wrong.

decisions.decision: Community data is read live from the remote, never mirrored into research.db.
decisions.why: Mirroring puts it on the reader's disk, which makes it un-gateable.

decisions.decision: Plan is a separate axis from role.
decisions.why: A moderator on free can moderate; a paying reader isn't a researcher. A tier named 'admin' is only what's paid for.

decisions.decision: The last maintainer can't be demoted.
decisions.why: It would lock everyone out of administering the community.

glossary.feature: Something you DO (publish, review, establish, administer). Gated by role.
glossary.resource: Something you READ (the corpus, the community, a translation, a dictionary). Gated by plan.
glossary.tier: A rung on the plan ladder (plan_tiers). Higher rank unlocks more.
glossary.min_plan: A resource's requirement: a tier, 'free' (signed in), or NULL (public).
glossary.API token: mqrg_… — a revocable credential that acts as its user; how the MCP signs in.
glossary.locally established: A form meaning YOU established, in your own research.db.
glossary.globally established: The reading moderators accepted as the group's; lives on the cloud.
glossary.dissent: A recorded disagreement with a globally established reading, preserved not resolved.
glossary.divergence (⚖): A form you established whose meaning differs from the group's. Computed live on the remote.

Offline reading in the app: today it needs the research server. A signed local cache of the corpus is possible later if wanted.
Corpus patches: the signed patch channel still targets quran.db; a Postgres target is needed for corrections to reach the cloud copy.
